prompt.context: Euro Logistics is a large logistics company. They want to improve their customer satisfaction index.
prompt.question: What should Euro Logistics do to improve their customer satisfaction index?

clarifying_info.q: How do customers currently evaluate Euro Logistics' service level?
clarifying_info.a: Provide Exhibit A — a customer satisfaction survey filled by over 250 companies across multiple European countries, showing scores for Billing, Customer Service, Order Tracking, and Delivery Time. Scores above 75 are considered good.

clarifying_info.q: What does the Billing score measure?
clarifying_info.a: Bills should be provided within 30 days before due date without any billing mistakes. Mistakes or delays reduce the score.

clarifying_info.q: What does the Customer Service score measure?
clarifying_info.a: All orders are received through a call center, which also answers customer questions. Delays in answering calls and/or failing to provide accurate information reduces the score.

clarifying_info.q: What does the Order Tracking score measure?
clarifying_info.a: This is an online tool that allows customers to track their shipments in real time. Lagged information or lack of detailed information reduces the score.

clarifying_info.q: What does the Delivery Time score measure?
clarifying_info.a: Shipments are expected to be delivered on-schedule without delay. Any delay reduces the score.

exhibits.title: Customer Satisfaction Survey
exhibits.shows: Bar charts for 9 European countries (Sweden, Italy, Ireland, Germany, Netherlands, England, Norway, France, Scotland) showing satisfaction scores (0–100) for their top-rated service dimensions. Each country chart lists dimensions in order of importance to that country's customers. A score above 75 is considered good.

framework: Map the customer value chain end-to-end: order placement → billing → shipment → delivery → post-delivery support
Identify customer satisfaction dimensions: Billing accuracy/timeliness, Customer Service responsiveness, Order Tracking visibility, Delivery Time reliability
Assess current performance against a benchmark (score of 75) across all dimensions and geographies
Prioritize improvement areas by combining importance weight (how many countries rate it as top concern) and current score gap
Evaluate feasibility and cost of closing each gap (technology investment, process redesign, third-party dependencies)
Quantify financial impact: reduction in churn, revenue retention, and payback period of investments

questions.prompt: [Present Exhibit A] What can you conclude from this table? Is there a particular country or measurement that should be of focus?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies: (1) Billing scores are below 75 in nearly every country and Billing is ranked as a top-priority dimension by most countries — making it the highest-priority gap. (2) Order Tracking also scores poorly and is cited as important in multiple countries. (3) Customer Service is important to most countries and generally scores well — not a priority fix. (4) Delivery Time has some low scores but delays are caused by customs, which is outside Euro Logistics' control; the only lever is setting more realistic delivery timelines.

questions.prompt: Euro Logistics wants to improve its Billing and Order Tracking systems. It will cost €5M each (total €10M). The new systems are estimated to reduce churn rate by 20%. Should they invest? What is the payback period?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate revenue at risk from churn, estimate savings from churn reduction, derive payback period, and compare against the goal of under 2 years. Recommendation: invest, because payback is ~1 year 4 months, well under the 2-year goal.

math.setup: Revenue lost per year = Current Revenue × Churn Rate; Savings = Revenue lost × Churn reduction; Payback = Investment ÷ Annual Savings
steps: Payback period = €10M ÷ €7.5M ≈ 1.33 years ≈ 1 year and 4 months
math.answer: Payback period ≈ 1 year 4 months, which is under the 2-year goal. Euro Logistics should proceed with the investment.

recommendation: Euro Logistics should invest €10M to upgrade both the Billing and Order Tracking systems, as this directly addresses the lowest-scoring and most widely-cited customer satisfaction gaps
The investment pays back in approximately 1 year and 4 months — well within the 2-year target — by reducing annual churn from 25% to 20%, saving €7.5M per year
risks: Churn reduction estimate of 20% may be optimistic; actual savings could be lower if dissatisfaction stems from factors beyond these two systems
Systems implementation may take time, delaying the start of savings realization
Delivery Time remains a concern in some markets; since customs delays are external, proactive communication and realistic deadline-setting are needed to manage expectations
next_steps: Initiate procurement or build process for new Billing and Order Tracking systems
Set realistic delivery timelines to partially address Delivery Time scores
Monitor churn rate quarterly post-implementation to validate the 20% reduction assumption
Consider a deeper root-cause analysis of Delivery Time delays and work with customs authorities or logistics partners where feasible
